subject.title: Clarify or preserve skill source provenance from CLI publish

question: Should CLI publish source flags remain non-visible metadata, become explicitly unverified public attribution, or gain a server-verified provenance workflow?
rationale: The answer determines what users may trust, which data can be exposed publicly, and whether verification needs new ownership and artifact-matching guarantees; source inspection cannot safely infer that policy.

options.title: Document non-provenance semantics
options.body: Keep current storage and trust behavior, but make CLI help and publish documentation state that these flags do not create GitHub-backed or trusted provenance.

options.title: Expose unverified attribution
options.body: Return a distinct, visibly unverified attribution field while keeping Skill Card and verify trust decisions limited to server-resolved provenance.

options.title: Design verified CLI provenance
options.body: Add a dedicated server verification protocol for repository access and claimed commit/path-to-upload correspondence before storing trusted provenance.

recommendation.title: Expose unverified attribution
recommendation.body: Return a distinct, visibly unverified attribution field while keeping Skill Card and verify trust decisions limited to server-resolved provenance.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged GitHub-backed source sync implementation is the closest established ownership trail for the server-resolved provenance model.
